When emulating an atomic access on behalf of the guest
gfn dirty if the CMPXCHG by KVM is attempted and doesn't fault.  This
fixes a bug where KVM effectively corrupts guest memory during live
migration by writing to guest memory without informing userspace that the
page is dirty.
Marking the page dirty got unintentionally dropped when KVM's emulated
CMPXCHG was converted to do a user access.  Before that
mapped the guest page into kernel memory
column2: and marked the page dirty during

column1: the unmap phase.
Mark the page dirty even if the CMPXCHG fails
column2: as the old data is written

column1: back on failure
column2: i.e. the page is still written.  The value written is

column1: guaranteed to be the same because the operation is atomic
is that all writes are dirty logged regardless of the value written.  And
more importantly
column2: that's what KVM did before the buggy commit.

column1: Huge kudos to the folks on the Cc list (and many others)
actual work of triaging and debugging.
